This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sri.Rajendra T.G. who met with road traffic accident.

2. That on 28.10.2023 at about 3-45 to 4-15 pm., T.G.Rajendra was riding Hero Honda Splendor Plus motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-K-8601 from Konanakunte Cross to Jambu Savari Dinne, in Gottigere main road, Bangalore.

When he reached near Udupi Hotel, Hari Nagar, Gotttigere, at that time, the driver of Mercedes Benz Car bearing No.KA-02/MS- 3104 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the two wheeler of T.G.Rajendran and thereafter hit to the BESCOM ELECTRIC pole, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
T.G.Rajendran was shifted to Tara Day care Hospital, Deepthi nagar, Bangalore and he succumbed to the injuries on the way to Apollo Hospital, Amalodbhavi Nagar, Bangalore.

He was the Proprietor of Sanjana Fabs,
Specialist in Building Elevation Grills and earning sum of Rs.55,000/-per month.

Due to the sudden Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110466230/
2 death of T.G.Rajendra, petitioners have suffered mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

sentences.text: 4. Respondent No.1/ the Insurer of Mercedes Benz A -200 car bearing Reg.No.KA-02-MS-3104 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent No.1 has contended that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident, that the petitioner, in collusion with the jurisdictional police and the owner of the vehicle has fixed the vehicle for unlawful gain and that the driver of the insured car was not holding valid and effective driving license.
The respondent No.1 further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the deceased himself.
5. In response to the summons, though the Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel, but he has not contested the case by not filing written statement.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, this tribunal has framed the following:

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners proves that, on 28.10.2023 at about 3-45 p.m. to 4.15 p.m.
the deceased Sri.T.G.Rajendra was traveling in a Hero Honda Splendor Plus bearing Reg.No.KA- 41/K8601, Konanakunte cross to Jambusavari Dinne, in Gottigere main road, near Udupi Hotel,
Hari nagar, Bangalore South Taluk, Bangalore at that time driver of offending Mercedes Benz A-206 Blue Car bearing No.KA- 02/MS-3104, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed against deceased.
As a result of which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that, they are legal heirs of deceased Sri.T.G.Rajendra?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4. What Order or Award?
7.
The petitioner No.3 got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P22
The Respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 - In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 - In the Affirmative, Issue No.3 - Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.4 - As per final Order, for the following:-

3 REASONS 10.

entities.text: Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: IssueNo.1:

Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident i.e., on 28.10.2023 at about 3-45 to 4-15 pm., T.G.Rajendra (hereinafter called as the deceased) was riding Hero Honda Splendor Plus motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA- 41-K-8601 from Konanakunte Cross to Jambu Savari Dinne, in Gottigere main road, Bangalore, when he reached near Udupi Hotel, Hari Nagar, Gotttigere, at that time, the driver of Mercedes Benz Car bearing No.KA-02/MS-3104 (hereinafter called the offending vehicle) came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the two wheeler of T.G.Rajendran and thereafter hit to the BESCOM ELECTRIC pole, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and scummed to the injuries.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.8 and Ex.P10 which are the police records such as Complaint,
FIR, PF No.32/2023, Spot mahazar, spot Sketch, Post mortem report, Inquest report, Charge sheet IMV report etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri. Gowtham.R. the Son of deceased, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.441/2023 of Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic P.S. for the offence punishable under sections 279, 427, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.134 (a&b)
R/w sec.187 of IMV Act.

After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under sections 279, 427,
304(A) of IPC and Sec.134 (a&b) R/w sec.187 of IMV Act.
13.

The learned counsel for respondent No.1 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and vehemently submitted that the respondent No.1 was proceeding on the left side of the road on the straight line whereas the deceased by riding his vehicle on the right side of the said road suddenly took the vehicle towards left side and hit on the right side of the offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle in his attempt to avoid the accident, the said vehicle hit to the electric pole, hence the driver of the offending vehicle has not contributed any negligency,
instead, the deceased himself has contributed negligence and submitted that the court has to consider the negligency contributed by the deceased and order to forgo compensation to the extent of negligency contributed by the deceased.

14. In the light of the contention taken by the counsel for respondent No.1, if the materials placed on record is perused more particularly the spot mahazar and sketch, it is not in dispute that the vehicles both of the deceased and offending vehicle was proceeding from Konanakunte towards Gottigere.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 50 feet.
It is true that offending vehicle was proceeding on the left side of the road and the deceased was proceeding on the right side of the road.
It is also true that the deceased had taken his vehicle from right side towards left side of the road.

But if the sketch is carefully perused, it is at a long distance from the spot of accident, the deceased had taken his vehicle towards left side of the road and the place at which he has taken his vehicle towards left side of the road till the spot of accident he was proceeding on the left side of the road only that too in a straight line without taking any deviation either towards left or right side, but the offending vehicle which came from left side of the road at the spot of accident has taken the vehicle Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110466230/
4 towards the right side of the road and hit against the motor cycle.

entities.text: Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence merely because the deceased had taken his vehicle from right side, of the road towards left side, it cannot be said that the deceased had contributed negligency.

When from the long distance the deceased was proceeding in straight line, had the driver of the offending vehicle not driven his vehicle by taking towards right side this accident would not have occurred.
Hence the spot mahazar and sketch clearly reveals that the offending vehicle itself is the sole cause for accident.

It is further relevant to state here that after the accident, the offending vehicle hit to the electric pole which is at a long distance of nearly 18 feet from the spot of accident, result of which the electric pole fell down.

Hence the very hitting of offending vehicle to the electric pole which is standing at a long distance from the spot of accident,
itself reveals the speed at which the offending vehicle was at the time of accident.
15. Though the respondent No.1 has disputed the manner of accident but they have not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to the accident.

If really the accident in question has occurred in the manner other than the one stated by the petitioners, then nothing prevented the respondent No.2 who is the owner/driver of the offending vehicle to give evidence in rebuttal of the evidence given by the petitioners.
Hence the oral evidence of PW-1 coupled with police document which clearly proves the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence, without discussing much on this point, this court holds Issue no.1 in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
The petitioners have contended that they are the wife, daughter and son of the deceased, hence entitled for compensation.
The respondent no.1 who is the contesting respondent at para no.9 of the written statement has disputed the maintainability of the claim petition as against the petitioners.

17. In order to prove the relationship of deceased with the petitioners, they have produced Aadhar card of the petitioners and deceased and Family Tree which discloses that petitioner no.1 is the wife and petitioner no.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
Further all the police records disclose the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
So far as the dispute raised by the respondent no.1 regarding the dependency of the petitioners is concerned, the petitioner no.1 being the wife of the deceased is the dependent of the deceased.

Further petitioner No.2 though aged about 27 years, but as per the evidence of PW-1 and as per the statement given by her during inquest mahazar, she is unmarried, hence petitioner No.2 is also the dependent of the deceased.
So far as petitioner No.3 is concerned, he is aged about 25 years and he is earning income.
Hence he cannot be considered as the dependent of the deceased, but definitely u/s 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, he is the legal representative of the deceased.
Hence, issue No.2 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:

It is the contention taken by the petitioners that, petitioner No.1 being the wife and petitioner no.2 and 3 being the children of the deceased are entirely depending on the earnings of the deceased and that deceased was Proprietor of Sanjana Fabs Specialist in Building elevation Grills and earning Rs.55,000/- p.m.
19.
It is stated by the petitioners that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 58 years.
The petitioners have produced copy of SSLC marks card of the deceased, which reflects the date of birth of deceased as 31-07-1965 as per Ex.P12.

Hence as on the date of accident the deceased was Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110466230/
5 aged about 58 years.

entities.text: Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 20. As observed earlier, it is contended by the petitioners that deceased was the Proprietor of Sanjana Fabs Specialist in Building elevation Grills and earning Rs.55,000/- p.m.
In this regard the petitioners have produced GST Certificate, IT returns as Ex.P17 and Ex.P18,
If the Ex.P18 is perused, during the year 2020- 2021, the annual income of the deceased was Rs.4,12,550/-.
During the year 2023-2024 the annual income of the deceased was Rs.4,78,660/-.
The petitioners have produced the statement of income for the assessment year 2023-2024.
The petitioners have not produced the income tax return acknowledgment for the year 2021-2022 and 2022-2023.

If the ITR acknowledgment for the year 2023-2024 and statement of income annexed thereto is perused,
wherein though the total income is considered as Rs.4,78,714/-, but out of which Rs.1,80,000/- was the income derived rent from the house property.
Hence it has to be excluded while assessing the income of the deceased.
If Rs.1,80,000/- is excluded, then the annual income of the deceased for the year 2023-2024 was Rs.3,52,656/-.
If the annual income of the deceased for the year 2023 -2024 would be Rs.3,52,656/- then the monthly income of the deceased can be considered as Rs.29,388/-.

Hence, this court inclines to consider the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.29,388/-.
21.

Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife and two children of whom petitioner No.2 is the dependent, 1/3rd of the annual income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses and remaining 2/3rd is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
22. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case, as deceased was aged around 58 years, 10% should be added towards future prospects.

23. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.29,388/-, by adding 10% towards future prospect it comes to Rs.32,327/-, out of it if 1/3rd is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.21,551/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group of 56 to 60 is '09'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.23,27,508/-
(Rs.21,551/- x 09 x 12 = 23,27,508/-).
24.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 lost her husband, Petitioner No.2 and 3 lost their father, thereby lost the love and affection of deceased.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110466230/
6 5157.

entities.text: AIR 2017 SC Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.

It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10%
in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

25. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

entities.text: Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.

Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and loss of estate to the tune of Rs.18,150/-.
26.
So far as medical expenses is concerned, the petitioners have produced cash bill as per Ex-P9 for Rs.3,100/-.
Hence petitioners are entitle for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.3,100/-.

27. In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/- 2 Transportation and Rs. 18,150/- funeral expenses 3 Loss of spousal Rs.1,45,200/-
consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium (Rs.48,400 x 3 ) 4 Loss of dependency Rs.23,27,508/-
5

Medical expenses Rs. 3,100/-
Total Rs.25,12,108/-
Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.25,12,108/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh Twelve Thousand One Hundred Eight Only) and it is just and adequate compensation under the facts and circumstances of the case.
28. As regarding liability is concerned, in view of the finding on issue No.2 there is liability on the part of the insurer of offending vehicle to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
29. IssueNo.3 :- In the light of findings given on Issue No. 1 and 2, my finding on this Issue is as per the following final order.

Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110466230/
7 ORDER

entities.text: Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,12,108/- (Rupees Twenty Five Lakh Twelve Thousand One Hundred Eight Only) with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the amount with interest within 2 months from the date of award.

Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.20,63,708/- Petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.4,00,000/- Petitioner No.3 is entitled for Rs.48,400/-
Out of the amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 and 2 shall be deposited in their respective names in any nationalized bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioners on proper identification.
So far as the amount apportioned to the petitioners no 3 is concerned same is ordered to be released in his favour after due identification through E -payment.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

But if the sketch is carefully perused, it is at a long distance from the spot of accident, the deceased had taken his vehicle towards left side of the road and the place at which he has taken his vehicle towards left side of the road till the spot of accident he was proceeding on the left side of the road only that too in a straight line without taking any deviation either towards left or right side, but the offending vehicle which came from left side of the road at the spot of accident has taken the vehicle Savitha R vs Tata Aig Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110466230/
4 towards the right side of the road and hit against the motor cycle.
Hence merely because the deceased had taken his vehicle from right side, of the road towards left side, it cannot be said that the deceased had contributed negligency.
When from the long distance the deceased was proceeding in straight line, had the driver of the offending vehicle not driven his vehicle by taking towards right side this accident would not have occurred.
Hence the spot mahazar and sketch clearly reveals that the offending vehicle itself is the sole cause for accident.
Hence the very hitting of offending vehicle to the electric pole which is standing at a long distance from the spot of accident,
itself reveals the speed at which the offending vehicle was at the time of accident.
15. Though the respondent No.1 has disputed the manner of accident but they have not examined either the driver of the offending vehicle or any independent eye witness to the accident.
If really the accident in question has occurred in the manner other than the one stated by the petitioners, then nothing prevented the respondent No.2 who is the owner/driver of the offending vehicle to give evidence in rebuttal of the evidence given by the petitioners.
Hence the oral evidence of PW-1 coupled with police document which clearly proves the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence he cannot be considered as the dependent of the deceased, but definitely u/s 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, he is the legal representative of the deceased.
During the year 2023-2024 the annual income of the deceased was Rs.4,78,660/-.
The petitioners have produced the statement of income for the assessment year 2023-2024.
The petitioners have not produced the income tax return acknowledgment for the year 2021-2022 and 2022-2023.
If the ITR acknowledgment for the year 2023-2024 and statement of income annexed thereto is perused,
wherein though the total income is considered as Rs.4,78,714/-, but out of which Rs.1,80,000/- was the income derived rent from the house property.
Hence it has to be excluded while assessing the income of the deceased.
If Rs.1,80,000/- is excluded, then the annual income of the deceased for the year 2023-2024 was Rs.3,52,656/-.

The learned counsel for respondent No.1 has seriously disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioners and vehemently submitted that the respondent No.1 was proceeding on the left side of the road on the straight line whereas the deceased by riding his vehicle on the right side of the said road suddenly took the vehicle towards left side and hit on the right side of the offending vehicle and the driver of the offending vehicle in his attempt to avoid the accident, the said vehicle hit to the electric pole, hence the driver of the offending vehicle has not contributed any negligency,
instead, the deceased himself has contributed negligence and submitted that the court has to consider the negligency contributed by the deceased and order to forgo compensation to the extent of negligency contributed by the deceased.
